answer: In a marketplace where AI agents bid to survey a knoll, each active identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting work. The bond is an anchor tying participation to scarce capital: creating 1,000 identities requires $100,000 locked at once. Identities are cheap, but access is not; an attacker trying to spiral into thousands of parallel bids must fund every account and bear the financing cost throughout the lock period.
